title: QCDIAG: addressing header field issue and other improvements
description:
Changes:
- Addressing the header field issue mentioned in !23600
- Introducing `qcdiag_data_t`
- Updating `qcdiag_add_cmd_hdr()`
- Updating `dissect_qcdiag_custom()`
- Adding `dissect_qcdiag_log()`
- Optimizing `request` bool value setting
- Fixing Coverity Resource leaks related to `timestamp`

Examples (updated): [qcdiag.pcapng](/uploads/8148f7eb18e642fb1c689b8d981ccc13/qcdiag.pcapng), [qcdiag_log.pcapng](/uploads/843ddb34595ef951e2081da06f4ca23f/qcdiag_log.pcapng)

Additional participants: @laf0rge, @osmith42, @lynxis, @martin.r.mathieson

Did you intend that this field might have a different meaning for each message type (log being one) ?

at the moment I just use this struct to mark the packet as custom. It could change again in the near future once more code is added.

For now this just follows your recommendation and I use `dissector_try_uint_with_data()`
Why not just skip the byte here?  Then you don't need to pass any info through the data param?

My logic is different for now. Since there is a large number of logcodes and it will take time to add to the WS code, I wanted to have the interim flexibility to have a "custom" option and be able to add packet with `data-text-lines` instead of not having anything to show/decode. This is valid for both command and log codes.

`DIAG_LOG_F` has more fields to decode before `data-text-lines` and I use the newly introduced structure to tell `qcdiag_log` to handle the packet as custom, meaning to use `data-text-lines`. Again, this part of the code related to custom packets can easily be changes and/or improved in the near future.
You can see comments for many functions where I tried to add details of the packet/byte structure and that should help you to understand the decoding logic I implemented.

I'm still not clear about what the 'custom' bool means.  Could you try to add a comment to say that it means?  You use it to skip a byte in one case, then in another place you basically do:

if custom show-data-as-generic-string-lines

Okay, there are 2 logical categories:

1. a certain command code (or log code if cmd code was 16/0x10) is decoded, dissect function is implemented
2. a certain command code (or log code if cmd code was 16/0x10) is **not** decoded yet so then let's allow the user (whoever created the pcap file) to use a custom packet for with line-based text data to be able to show something as an alternative option.

With this logic we do not limit down to only show packets which are implemented already, we allow to have a basic text line based representation of unimplemented messages. this gives a better flexibility overall.

Packet 12 in qcdiag.pcpang is an example, but not so good example (since it's only 1 line of text).

```
Qualcomm Diagnostic, Get Log Response, Unknown Log Code (0x4125)
    Command Code: Get Log (0x10)
    Length: 46 bytes
    Log Code: Unknown (0x4125)
    More log data available indicator: 0
    Log Message Length: 46 bytes
    Timestamp: Jan  6, 1980 07:00:00.000000000 SE Asia Standard Time
    Unknown Log Code (0x4125)
        Line-based text data (1 lines)
            WCDMA RRC State: CONNECTING (1)
```

this shows a log code packet 0x4125 which:
- does not have the logcode with name implemented yet (hence, Unknown)
- uses the line-based text data to still show what the packet actually means

Additionally, if a logcode does not have a fully validated decoding logic, perhaps it's better to use the Line-based text data option instead of a wrong decoding implementation.
As of now, the custom bool is simply used to flag the packet to be decoded as `line-based text data` in packet-qcdiag_log.c. I do not see a better and simpler way for that.
I guess this interface will settle down once you add any more subdissectors..
For the overall value, wouldn't 0x%08x  be more readable?

The version is stored 1 or 4 bytes and can be referred with the integer value or the actual major.minor representation. I wanted to add both together which is more user friendly. This is Qualcomm's logic of versioning.

For example:
- Version 1 (1) -- e.g LTE log codes (single digit)
- Version 131072 (2.0) -- e.g. NR log codes
- Version 196608 (3.0) -- e.g. NR log codes
- Version 196618 (3.10) -- e.g. NR log codes

`0x%08x` would not help to read the version easily.
My point here is that 196618 can be shown as 0x0003000A which makes the breakdown (3.10) more obvious.

I follow the Qualcomm `[Version xxx]` representation, and I thought I should not change that. If Qualcomm shares as `[Version 196618]` and the Packet Bytes view shows the bytes `0x0003000A` then why would I change? That is why I made `Version: 196618 (3.10)`. Does it make sense?
Ok.  You could show both, but its up to you.

For me since the bytes `0x0003000A` can be easily seen in the Packet Bytes View, I would not add it to the tree, for me it's redundant. It makes sense to me to use the integer value (which is also used by Qualcomm) and "decode" it too and add that in brackets. 

Hence: `Version: 196618 (3.10)`

This seems overly complicated, I've never felt the need to do anything like this.

I don't see the need for separate hf_diag_ver and hf_qcdiag_log_len - you could just have the 4-byte entry and set the value you need.

Does the version (in your capture, value 1) really belong to 'LTE NAS EMM...', or does it belong to qcdiag_log ?  The layering is confusing generally to me - I loaded your new capture and filtered for qcdiag_log and no frames matched - you add some fields (more, length, ts, ver) but never add the protocol root itself, so the filter doesn't match.  It is surprising to see within the same 'Qualcomm Diagnostic' subtree some 'qcdiag' fields, then switching over to 'qcdiag_log'.

I think @laf0rge said that the range of these messages is vast - is there a case for folding this \_log part into 'qcdiag' itself?  This would reduce the layering confusing - and surely the most central/useful thing this dissector can do is to read the context for, then dissect familiar standards-based PDUs?

Presumably there may be some other codes (within qcdiag_log) that also have a version field at the start, that may be 1 or 4 bytes?  Why not just let individual cases handle this version field if they have it?  They could always add it outside of the subtree they will create for their own data.

Versions only valid for log codes, only under `Get Log (16/0x10)` command.

Log code versioning was introduced with LTE codes as far as I understand, but it was on 1 byte, single digit, e.g. [Version 1]. Yes, the log codes might have versions, some of them evolved by time and had multiple versions:

```
0xB0C8	LTE RRC Idle Meas Config Info  [Version 5]
0xB0C9	LTE RRC Logged Meas Config
0xB0CA	LTE RRC Log Meas Info [Version 2]
0xB0CB	LTE RRC Paging UE [Version 2]
0xB0CD	LTE RRC Supported CA Combos [Version 40, 41]
0xB0D1	LTE RRC Cap Related Info [Version 40]
0xB0D3	LTE RRC Connection Release Info [Version 1]
```

But then for 1x and NR log codes the version is stored on 4 bytes, e.g. [Version 196608] (which is version 3.0):

```
0xB821	NR5G RRC OTA Packet
0xB822	NR5G RRC MIB Info [Version 131072]
0xB823	NR5G RRC Serving Cell Info [Version 196611]
0xB825	NR5G RRC Configuration Info [Version 196618]
0xB826	NR5G RRC Supported CA Combos [Version 24]
0xB827	NR5G RRC PLMN Search Request [Version 4]
```

When I dissect "Get Log Response" messages, in `dissect_qcdiag_log()` I add `hf_qcdiag_ver` before dealing with the command code. Perhaps here I could add a logic to decide the size of version based on command code? Would that be better? But for now I cannot validate for all log codes so I thought whichever log code has a function to dissect, we can decide within the particular function what size of version (1 or 4 bytes) could be used.

Having all in one file would be much more complex I believe. In some other decoding tools (e.g. SCAT) even the qcdiag_log is separated based on the log code base (equipment ID).

The Get Log (16/0x10) command log has all the logcodes covered and it makes sense to separate from the rest of the code. But I think it's even more helpful during the development to avoid mix ups with the rest of the code.

What is the layering confusion? This is a clear separation of `Get Log (16/0x10)` command since it has a cast amount of log command underneath to be decoded.

Please also note, the structure of the log code packets (Get Log (16/0x10)) are set by Qualcomm and I just decode it. You can see in the comment above `dissect_qcdiag_log()` in `packet-qcdiag_log.c` which shows the structure.

The `DATA` in the Response might start with 1 or 4 bytes of version depending on the log code. This is how Qualcomm designed it.

I have not added NR log code related dissect functions yet so you cannot compare and see the reason behind of this code for 1/4 bytes of version. 

I go step by step and with smaller changes to make sure it can be reviewed and mistakes corrected. Also, it takes time to write the code actually :smile:

changed this line in [version 4 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23619/diffs?diff_id=1668305573&start_sha=32a3eb23509b6ed35afc4ef8775551374394b208#3f9bf15cbd698a6492dccf1870b37f8bad11b013_599_584)

I revised the version related code and made it simpler. `hf_qcdiag_ver` will be only added when it's really needed (in individual dissect functions).

`hf_qcdiag_ver_4` will be used for NR log codes in another MR.

I do prefer that you moved the dissection of the version out to where you know for certain that it appears and what width it will be.

When I mentioned layering, I meant that when you open a frame (say, frame 9 in qcdiag_log.pcapng), inside the "qcdiag" layer, as you go down the fields you go from "qcdiag.logcode" to "qcdiag_log.more" at the same level. I am used to seeing a subtree (with a protocol root) being added when we move down into another protocol layer. Another consequence of not having a protocol root is that the display filter "qcdiag_log" doesn't match with anything in that capture file.

If you would really rather not introduce a subtree with qcdiag_log, that's probably OK, but I think do add a hidden protocol root at least so that the "qcdiag_log" filter works.

I corrected this yesterday in a way which make much more sense.

Only some logcodes have `Version` hence, the Version hf shall be under the log code.

For example, in case of `LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (Downlink)` the Version shall be inside of that, before the Release version.

```
Qualcomm Diagnostic, Get Log Response, LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (Downlink)
    Command Code: Get Log (0x10)
    Length: 19 bytes
    Log Code: LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (0xb0ec)
    More log data available indicator: 0
    Log Message Length: 19 bytes
    Timestamp: Mar 20, 2024 15:38:21.134006738 SE Asia Standard Time
    LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (Downlink)
        Version: 1 (1) <---
        Release Version: 9.5.0
```
Saw that, yes.

My logic here was:
```
Qualcomm Diagnostic, <Command Code Request/Response>, <Log Code name> (Uplink/Downlink)
```
the following 3 are generic Command Code HFs:
```
    Command Code: Get Log (0x10)
    Length: 19 bytes
    Log Code: LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (0xb0ec)
```
since this is command code `Get Log Response`, we have additional HFs:
```
    More log data available indicator: 0
    Log Message Length: 19 bytes
    Timestamp: Mar 20, 2024 15:38:21.134006738 SE Asia Standard Time
```
The log code itself may have more HFs so we add those too:
```
    LTE NAS EMM Plain OTA Incoming Message (Downlink)
        Version: 1 (1)
        Release Version: 9.5.0
```
